name: Salesforce
one_liner: Salesforce has a broad REST/SOAP/Bulk/GraphQL API with OAuth2 and a free Developer Edition org, but its API terms require ISV Partner Program enrollment for commercial multi-customer use; vendor also offers MCP servers.
blocker_notes: A free Developer Edition org gives working OAuth credentials, so building and testing is self-serve. But the SFDC API Terms bar Commercial Use of the APIs unless the app is enrolled in Salesforce's ISV partner program, which applies to a commercial multi-tenant toolkit.

name: HubSpot
one_liner: HubSpot has a broad REST API with self-serve OAuth2 apps, free developer accounts, service keys/private tokens, and an official remote MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com.
blocker_notes: No blocker; free developer account allows building and testing.

name: Pipedrive
one_liner: Pipedrive has a broad REST API (v1/v2) with self-serve OAuth 2.0 app registration, API tokens, a free developer sandbox, and an official MCP server, so a toolkit is buildable now.
blocker_notes: Nothing major. The sandbox is requested rather than instant, but the 14-day trial and API tokens on every plan are fallbacks. The daily token budget is a rate limit, not friction.

name: Attio
one_liner: Attio CRM has a broad public REST API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 and API keys, free-plan API access, webhooks, an OpenAPI spec and an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: No meaningful blocker. Free workspace gives API access and OAuth app registration is self-serve.

name: Twenty
one_liner: Twenty is an open-source CRM with REST and GraphQL APIs, OAuth 2.0 with self-serve dynamic client registration, API keys, and an official MCP server. Builders can get credentials from a free self-hosted instance or a cloud trial.
blocker_notes: No real blocker. A free self-hosted instance or a cloud trial is enough to build and test. The API schema is per workspace and includes custom objects, so the toolkit should discover the schema at runtime.

name: Podio
one_liner: Podio has a free-to-use REST API with self-serve OAuth2 app registration, broad coverage, and an official hosted MCP server at mcp.podio.com.
blocker_notes: No blocker found. The free plan includes API access, and API key registration is self-serve.

name: Zoho CRM
one_liner: Zoho CRM has a broad REST API (v8) with OAuth 2.0 auth-code flow, free plan/Developer Edition for self-serve credentials, and vendor-published MCP servers.
blocker_notes: Minor: data-center-specific URLs, per-org tokens, credit-based rate limits; none are blockers.

name: Close
one_liner: Close is a CRM with a broad REST API, self-serve OAuth app registration, API keys, and an official remote MCP server. The builder can test with a 14-day trial or a free Dev org.
blocker_notes: No free plan; only a 14-day trial (or a Dev org requested from support). Under the rubric a trial under 30 days is friction.

name: Copper
one_liner: Copper CRM has a broad REST Developer API using API-key headers, but no free tier: API needs a Professional plan or a 14-day trial, and OAuth app registration requires emailing Copper. An official MCP server is announced but still in waitlist beta.
blocker_notes: API needs Professional or higher, or the 14-day trial, which is short for ongoing toolkit testing. Self-serve OAuth is not available because app registration goes through partners@copper.com.

name: DealCloud
one_liner: DealCloud (Intapp) is a CRM for financial services with a broad REST API (OAuth2 client credentials plus a user-generated API key) and an official MCP server, but it is sold via sales and has no self-serve signup or trial.
blocker_notes: No public signup or sandbox is documented. Credentials require a licensed DealCloud tenant, obtained through sales or an account manager. The MCP server is per-tenant, needs a Celeste license, and does not support local clients such as Claude Code.

name: Zendesk
one_liner: Zendesk has a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 (auth code + PKCE); only a free 14-day trial gives working credentials, global OAuth for multi-tenant apps needs Zendesk approval; Zendesk now has its own official MCP server (via Zendesk Bridge, EAP).
blocker_notes: Only a 14-day trial is available without partnership. Multi-tenant distribution needs a global OAuth client approved by Zendesk. Per-instance OAuth clients are creatable in Admin Center.

name: Intercom
one_liner: Intercom has a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 for public apps, a free developer workspace with access tokens, and an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Free dev workspace gives working credentials. App review applies only to App Store publishing.

name: Freshdesk
one_liner: Freshdesk has a broad REST v2 API using an agent API key via Basic auth, plus a vendor-run MCP server; the free plan has no API access, so builders need a trial or paid plan.
blocker_notes: The API is unavailable on the free plan. A builder must use a limited trial (50 calls/min) or buy a paid plan to get a working key. Trial length is unverified.

name: Front
one_liner: Front has a documented REST Core API with OAuth2 apps and API tokens, a free developer sandbox account, and an official vendor MCP server.
blocker_notes: Public App Store listing requires partner approval; building and testing do not.

name: Pylon
one_liner: Pylon (usepylon.com) has a REST API with admin-created bearer tokens and an official MCP server (OAuth or API token), but API access needs a paid plan (Professional or higher).
blocker_notes: The API is documented, but a working token needs a paid Pylon workspace on Professional or higher. No free tier or trial appears in the fetched pages. A sales-assisted route may exist but is unverified.

name: LiveAgent
one_liner: LiveAgent helpdesk has a documented REST API v3 with admin-generated API keys, a 30-day free trial with no credit card, and a vendor-built MCP server (Business plan and up).
blocker_notes: A 30-day no-card trial is long enough to build and test the REST API. Each customer has its own domain and API key, which is not counted as friction under the rubric.

name: Plain
one_liner: Plain is a B2B support platform with a full GraphQL API, OAuth apps, machine-user API keys and an official hosted MCP server (400+ tools). The pages show no free tier or trial, so the builder probably needs a paid workspace, but this is unverified.
blocker_notes: No free plan or trial is shown in the evidence, so a paid workspace is probably needed to get credentials. A trial may exist but is not confirmed.

name: Help Scout
one_liner: Help Scout has a broad OAuth2 REST Mailbox API and an official MCP server, but API access requires a paid plan (Standard+), since the Free plan excludes it.
blocker_notes: The builder needs a paid Help Scout plan (Standard or above) to get API credentials. Reporting endpoints need Plus or Pro.

name: Gorgias
one_liner: Gorgias has a broad REST API (Basic auth with per-user API key; OAuth2 only for approved public apps) and an official MCP, but API access requires a paid helpdesk plan.
blocker_notes: Builder needs a paid Gorgias helpdesk account (trial not confirmed in the evidence) to obtain an API key. OAuth2 for multi-user needs partner app approval.

name: Gladly
one_liner: Gladly has a broad REST API with per-user API tokens (HTTP Basic) and an OpenAPI spec, but access requires a Gladly customer instance obtained via demo/sales; no self-serve signup or trial is documented.
blocker_notes: A builder needs a Gladly instance (demo/sales conversation) to get a sandbox or API token. No self-serve path is documented.

name: Slack
one_liner: Slack has a broad REST Web API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 app registration, a free developer sandbox, and an official Slack-hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: None for building; free developer sandbox and self-serve app creation are available.

name: Twilio
one_liner: Twilio has a broad REST API with a free trial (no card) giving working Account SID/Auth Token credentials; Basic auth is primary, and a vendor-hosted, docs-only MCP server exists.
blocker_notes: No real blocker; trial accounts have messaging restrictions and expire after 30 days, but upgrading is self-serve.

name: Zoho Cliq
one_liner: Zoho Cliq has a broad REST API v2/v3 with self-serve OAuth 2.0 via the Zoho API Console, a free plan with API support, and an official Zoho MCP server.
blocker_notes: Per-user rate limits and lock periods apply, and multiple data centers need handling, but neither blocks building.

name: Lark (Larksuite)
one_liner: Lark Open Platform offers a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 user authorization and tenant tokens, self-serve app creation, and an official MCP server (lark-mcp, local npm tool).
blocker_notes: Minor: scopes need tenant admin approval, and Starter caps basic API calls at 10,000/month; neither blocks building. The remote MCP server mode is marked deprecated and in internal testing, but the official local lark-mcp tool remains.

name: Pumble
one_liner: Pumble has a free, self-serve REST API (API-key addon plus OAuth2 app SDK) and an official hosted MCP server. A toolkit is buildable now.
blocker_notes: Minor: the OAuth app requires a public HTTP server for events, and the API key addon has limited endpoints. Neither blocks a toolkit.

name: Discord
one_liner: Discord has a broad, free REST API with OAuth2 for users and bot tokens, self-serve via the Developer Portal; only community MCP servers were found.
blocker_notes: Privileged intent review applies only past 10,000 users, which does not affect building or testing. Some scopes are partner-only.

name: Telegram
one_liner: Telegram offers a free Bot API (HTTPS, token from @BotFather) plus the MTProto Telegram API (api_id/api_hash); easily buildable, with only community MCP servers found.
blocker_notes: Bots cannot act as a user account; user-level access needs MTProto sessions. The fetched pages did not show any vendor MCP server (absence is not proof), and the community MCP evidence was not among the fetched pages, so the mcp label is kept at low confidence.

name: WhatsApp Business
one_liner: Meta's WhatsApp Business Cloud API is a broad Graph API REST surface; direct developers get a system-user token self-serve, but multi-tenant use needs Meta App Review (Advanced access) and Tech Provider status. Meta ships an official WhatsApp Business Tools MCP (beta).
blocker_notes: Building and testing against own assets is self-serve, but shipping a multi-tenant toolkit requires Meta App Review with Advanced access (and Tech Provider/Embedded Signup for onboarding customers).

name: Aircall
one_liner: Aircall has a broad REST API with self-serve Basic Auth API keys for any customer account; OAuth is limited to Tech Partners; an official read-only beta MCP exists but needs beta enrollment and the AI add-on.
blocker_notes: Basic Auth keys work with an Aircall account, which likely needs a trial or paid plan (trial terms unverified). Multi-user OAuth needs Tech Partner approval, so a multi-tenant OAuth toolkit is gated by that program; per-customer Basic keys are workable. The official MCP is read-only, beta, and needs beta enrollment via account manager plus the AI add-on.

name: Vonage
one_liner: Vonage offers self-serve REST communications APIs (SMS, Voice, Messages, Verify, Numbers, etc.) with API key/secret and JWT auth, free signup credit, and official MCP servers.
blocker_notes: Free account gives working credentials with demo credit; the VBC and RCS sub-products are gated but the core APIs are not.

name: Google Ads
one_liner: Google Ads API is a free, broad API (gRPC, REST) with OAuth2; production use requires per-Cloud-project access-level approval (Explorer is mostly automated), and an official MCP server exists.
blocker_notes: Production use needs Explorer/Basic/Standard access via Google's review. Test accounts and Test access allow building and testing meanwhile.

name: Meta Ads
one_liner: Meta's Marketing API (Graph API) for Facebook/Instagram ads is broad and OAuth2-capable, with an official hosted MCP server, but multi-user production use needs App Review, Advanced Access and Marketing API Full Access tier.
blocker_notes: Builders can test on their own ad accounts with standard access. Production multi-user OAuth needs Meta App Review (advanced access), Business Verification and Marketing API Full Access tier.

name: LinkedIn Ads
one_liner: LinkedIn Ads (Marketing/Advertising API) is a broad REST API with 3-legged OAuth2; apps are created self-serve but the Advertising API product requires LinkedIn approval, with the Development tier limited to editing 5 ad accounts.
blocker_notes: The Advertising API product requires LinkedIn approval; Standard tier requires a further upgrade for managing many accounts. Development tier is enough to build and test (5 editable ad accounts).

name: GoHighLevel
one_liner: GoHighLevel has a broad REST v2 API with OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens plus an official hosted MCP server; API access is bundled with paid plans (Starter $97/mo), with only a short trial reported.
blocker_notes: The builder needs a HighLevel subscription (Starter $97/month and up) or a short trial. Some endpoints need the Founder plan ($497/month).

name: Mailchimp
one_liner: Mailchimp Marketing API v3 is a broad REST API with self-serve API keys and OAuth 2 app registration on a free account; Mailchimp also publishes an official MCP server (for its Transactional/Mandrill API) plus a docs-search MCP, with community servers covering the Marketing API.
blocker_notes: No blocker. Account gives an API key and OAuth app registration.

name: Klaviyo
one_liner: Klaviyo has a broad REST API with self-serve private API keys and self-serve OAuth app creation, free test accounts, and an official vendor-hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Marketplace listing needs partner approval, but building and testing do not. Conversations API is reportedly gated.

name: systeme.io
one_liner: systeme.io has a REST public API authenticated with a self-generated X-API-Key, plus an official hosted MCP server (mcp.systeme.io) using MCP keys, available on all plans including Free.
blocker_notes: Per-user API keys are required rather than OAuth; this is not a blocker. Free-plan REST API access is not explicitly stated, but MCP is stated as available on the Free plan.

name: Pinterest
one_liner: Pinterest API v5 is a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0; it's free, but apps need Pinterest approval for Trial access and a video review for Standard access. An official MCP server is announced but not yet launched.
blocker_notes: Pinterest must approve the app for Trial access before an app ID and secret are issued. Multi-user production use needs Standard access, which requires a video review.

name: Threads (Meta)
one_liner: Threads API is a free REST Graph-style API with OAuth 2.0 user tokens; self-serve dev access works for testers, but multi-user use needs Meta App Review.
blocker_notes: Each permission needs Meta App Review (and app publishing) before arbitrary end users can authorize; development/testing is possible meanwhile with Threads testers.

name: SendGrid
one_liner: SendGrid has a broad REST v3 API with API-key Bearer auth; access is via a 60-day free trial (100 emails/day), and only community MCP servers were found.
blocker_notes: A 60-day trial is long enough to build and test. Customers use their own API keys. Vendor MCP status was not verifiable from the provided pages.

name: Shopify
one_liner: Shopify offers a broad GraphQL (plus legacy REST) Admin API with self-serve OAuth apps and free dev stores; ready to build, and the vendor publishes an official Shopify MCP for store management plus a dev-docs MCP.
blocker_notes: Some scopes and APIs need Shopify approval, but core development and testing are unblocked.

name: WooCommerce
one_liner: WooCommerce is a free, open-source WordPress plugin whose REST API (wc/v3) is authenticated with merchant-generated consumer key/secret, so a builder can self-host a store and test right away.
blocker_notes: Each user must supply their own store URL and generate keys. HTTPS is recommended and pretty permalinks are required. These are per-customer setup steps, not blockers for the builder.

name: BigCommerce
one_liner: BigCommerce offers a broad REST and GraphQL API. Free sandbox/trial stores give working API credentials, and the vendor has official MCP servers (Storefront, Store Management, WebMCP, Docs).
blocker_notes: Marketplace publishing needs an approved Technology Partner account, but that is not required to build and test a toolkit.

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
one_liner: Salesforce B2C Commerce exposes broad REST APIs (SCAPI/OCAPI) with Account Manager and SLAS OAuth tokens, and the vendor ships an official B2C MCP server. A real instance still comes through Salesforce, though a public demo sandbox exists.
blocker_notes: A B2C Commerce instance and realm are needed to create API clients. The only explicit access route in the evidence is contacting Salesforce sales. A demo sandbox is mentioned and might lower the barrier for shopper API testing, but this is unverified.

name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
one_liner: Magento Open Source is free and self-hosted with broad REST/GraphQL APIs; auth is per-store OAuth 1.0a integrations or tokens, with no central app registry or multi-tenant OAuth2.
blocker_notes: There is no hosted public sandbox. The builder must stand up their own Magento instance, and each merchant has its own base URL and OAuth 1.0a integration, so there is no central multi-user OAuth app flow.

name: Squarespace
one_liner: Squarespace has a broad REST Commerce API with per-site API keys (paid Commerce Advanced plan) and OAuth 2.0 (manual client review), plus an official remote MCP server; buildable with friction.
blocker_notes: Multi-user OAuth needs manual Squarespace approval of the OAuth client. Testing with API keys needs a paid Commerce Advanced site.

name: Ecwid
one_liner: Ecwid has a broad REST API with OAuth2 for public apps and non-expiring secret tokens for custom apps, but API access requires a paid store plan (free test-store upgrade available via email).
blocker_notes: API requires a paid Ecwid plan; the builder must email Ecwid API support to get a free test-store upgrade, or pay (Starter about $5/mo).

name: Gumroad
one_liner: Gumroad has a free, self-serve REST v2 API with OAuth2 app registration and personal access tokens, plus an official MCP server.
blocker_notes: None found. No sandbox; test with a throwaway account.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: Amazon SP-API is a broad REST API for seller/vendor data using LWA OAuth 2.0; builders need a Professional seller account ($39.99/mo) and Amazon-reviewed developer profile and role approvals.
blocker_notes: Developer profile review by Amazon and role approval, plus a paid Professional seller account, are required before meaningful use. Public multi-user apps need Appstore listing.

name: fanbasis
one_liner: FanBasis (now Commas) has a REST public API with x-api-key keys from the merchant dashboard, plus sandbox and webhooks; only a third-party Zapier MCP was found.
blocker_notes: None for building: FanBasis (now Commas) issues API keys from the merchant dashboard. Its MCP server is first-party (the commas-cli is a client for it).

name: DataForSEO
one_liner: DataForSEO offers a broad REST API for SEO data with Basic auth. Signup is free and includes a $1 trial credit plus a free sandbox. An official MCP server exists.
blocker_notes: No blocker. Free signup, a sandbox and trial credit are enough to build and test.

name: SE Ranking
one_liner: SE Ranking offers a broad REST Data/Project API with API-key auth, a 14-day trial with 100K credits, and an official vendor-hosted MCP server (OAuth 2.1 or API key).
blocker_notes: Only a 14-day trial (100K credits) is free; ongoing testing needs a paid plan or $50 PAYG credits. The trial is enough to build, so friction is modest.

name: Ahrefs
one_liner: Ahrefs API v3 is a broad REST API with bearer API keys, but it requires an eligible paid plan (Lite and up). Non-paid plans only get limited free test queries. It has an official hosted remote MCP server.
blocker_notes: Meaningful API access needs an eligible paid Ahrefs plan. Free test queries allow limited development. OAuth via Ahrefs Connect requires applying and approval. Ahrefs's MCP terms also forbid using the MCP endpoint through custom scripts or standalone clients.

name: MrScraper
one_liner: MrScraper has a REST scraping API with self-serve API tokens, a reported free tier, and an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: None found. The breadth rating is a judgement because no endpoint count was given. The free-tier claim rests on pages not re-fetched here.

name: Apify
one_liner: Apify has a broad REST API with API-token auth, webhooks, an OpenAPI spec and an official hosted MCP server (OAuth or token); free-plan access comes from draft evidence the fetched pages didn't confirm, so it is likely ready to build.
blocker_notes: No blocker is visible in the pages. Free credit limits are not a blocker.

name: Firecrawl
one_liner: Firecrawl has a hosted REST API (v2) with free self-serve API keys, OAuth 2.1 for apps, and an official MCP server.
blocker_notes: None. Free credits are limited but enough to build and test.

name: Bright Data
one_liner: Bright Data offers a REST API (Web Unlocker, SERP, Web Scraper, Scraper Studio) with bearer API key auth, a free tier of 5,000 monthly credits, and an official MCP server.
blocker_notes: No blocker. Free credits are a monthly allowance; the MCP server may require an Admin-permission API key.

name: Sherlock
one_liner: Sherlock (sherlock-project) is a local open-source CLI that checks usernames across sites with no hosted API, no credentials and only community MCP wrappers, so it doesn't fit a hosted-API toolkit.
blocker_notes: The tool only runs locally as a CLI that sends many web requests to third-party sites. There is no hosted API for Composio to call. A toolkit would need to host and run the tool itself.

name: Waterfall.io
one_liner: Waterfall.io offers a REST API for contact and company enrichment that uses an x-api-key header. Keys are issued only after the vendor approves a request, and pricing is quoted case by case.
blocker_notes: Keys are issued only after approval and a conversation with the team. Some endpoints are in preview or need access enabled on the key. The WP Waterfall MCP server and the Workato prebuilt "Waterfall Lead Enrichment" MCP server are unrelated to Waterfall.io (different company / a ZoomInfo-Apollo-LeadIQ workflow). The Waterfall.io docs pages seen mention agent skills but no MCP server. Only a subset of the docs was seen, so 'none' is kept at low confidence.

name: Clay
one_liner: Clay has a REST Public API (api.clay.com/public/v0) using a self-serve API key, reportedly available on all plans including Free, plus an official hosted MCP server at api.clay.com/v3/mcp with open OAuth DCR.
blocker_notes: Public API is limited in scope: it runs searches and routines/functions and works with audiences and signals. Table reads are Enterprise only. Writes to tables go through inbound webhooks.

name: GitHub
one_liner: GitHub offers a broad free REST (and GraphQL) API with self-serve OAuth apps and PATs, plus an official MCP server.
blocker_notes: Nothing blocks a build. Some features, such as Copilot, need paid plans, but that falls on end customers. Partner programs are optional.

name: Vercel
one_liner: Vercel has a broad REST API authenticated with self-serve access tokens that work on the free Hobby plan, and it has an official remote MCP server.
blocker_notes: None.

name: Netlify
one_liner: Netlify has a broad REST API with self-serve PATs and OAuth2 apps, a free plan, and an official MCP server; ready to build.
blocker_notes: None; free account gives credentials and OAuth app registration is self-serve.

name: Cloudflare
one_liner: Cloudflare has a broad REST API with self-serve API tokens, OAuth client management, and an official MCP server covering the whole API.
blocker_notes: No blocker for the core API.

name: Supabase
one_liner: Supabase has a free tier, a REST Management API with self-serve OAuth2 apps and per-project REST APIs, plus an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Free projects pause after a week of inactivity, which is minor.

name: Neo4j
one_liner: Neo4j offers the Aura management REST API (OAuth2 client credentials) plus per-database HTTP Query API (Basic/Bearer) and an official MCP server; the free Aura tier allows self-serve testing.
blocker_notes: Per-instance credentials, and no multi-user OAuth authorization-code flow. The partner program pages are for resellers and integrators and do not gate API access.

name: Snowflake
one_liner: Snowflake has a broad REST API surface (SQL API, Cortex) and an official managed MCP server; trial accounts give self-serve access, with PAT/OAuth/key-pair auth.
blocker_notes: Per-account URLs and admin-created OAuth integrations are customer-setup items. Trial length unconfirmed.

name: MongoDB Atlas
one_liner: MongoDB Atlas Administration API is a broad REST API with free self-serve service accounts (OAuth client-credentials, recommended) and legacy digest API keys; user-delegated OAuth is invite-only; official MCP exists.
blocker_notes: Self-serve credentials available today. Delegated OAuth is invite-only, but per-customer service accounts/API keys work.

name: Datadog
one_liner: Datadog has a broad REST API with self-serve API/app keys and PATs; OAuth exists but is limited to approved partners; an official remote MCP server exists; builder access is via a 14-day free trial.
blocker_notes: Builder access is via a short 14-day trial. Multi-user OAuth is limited to partner-registered clients, so the toolkit must use per-customer API/app keys or PATs.

name: Sentry
one_liner: Sentry has a broad REST API (sentry.io/api/0) with bearer auth tokens and OAuth for Sentry Apps. A free Developer plan is available, and there is an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Possible minor friction: third-party sources say the free plan excludes the API, but Sentry's docs point to a free developer account. The 14-day Business trial would also work.

name: Notion
one_liner: Notion has a broad REST API with free self-serve internal tokens, PATs and public OAuth, plus an official hosted MCP server; ready to build.
blocker_notes: No meaningful blocker; a free personal workspace provides owner rights for internal connections and PATs.

name: Airtable
one_liner: Airtable has a broad REST Web API with free-tier PATs and self-serve OAuth app registration, plus an official MCP server; ready to build.
blocker_notes: Free-plan call limits are low but workable for testing. Views endpoints are not on Free; Enterprise endpoints need Enterprise Scale.

name: Linear
one_liner: Linear has a broad GraphQL API with self-serve OAuth2 apps and personal API keys, included on the free plan, plus an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: None. A free workspace gives OAuth app registration and API keys.

name: Jira
one_liner: Jira Cloud has a broad REST v3 API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and basic/API-token auth, plus an official Atlassian Rovo MCP server.
blocker_notes: Tier 2 per-tenant rate limits require review, but apps start in Tier 1 and this does not block building a toolkit.

name: Asana
one_liner: Asana has a broad REST API with free self-serve PATs and OAuth 2.0 app registration, plus an official hosted MCP server; ready to build.
blocker_notes: Minor: some endpoints paid-only; not blocking.

name: Monday.com
one_liner: monday.com has a broad GraphQL API with self-serve OAuth apps, personal tokens, a free developer sandbox, and an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: None. Credentials are self-serve and free through the developer account.

name: ClickUp
one_liner: ClickUp has a broad public REST API available on all plans including free, with personal tokens and self-serve OAuth2 apps, plus an official remote MCP server (OAuth-only).
blocker_notes: Only minor limits: some endpoints Enterprise-only; OAuth app creation needs Workspace owner/admin.

name: Coda
one_liner: Coda has a free, broad REST API (v1) with personal API tokens, and an official hosted MCP server at coda.io/apis/mcp.
blocker_notes: None found. The Admin API is Enterprise-only, but the main v1 API is not.

name: Smartsheet
one_liner: Smartsheet has a broad REST API with OAuth2 and API tokens plus a vendor-run MCP server, but API and MCP access require a paid Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan.
blocker_notes: The builder needs a paid Smartsheet plan (Business or higher) to use the API, generate tokens and register OAuth apps.

name: Harvest
one_liner: Harvest (time tracking) v2 REST API is open to all accounts including free/trial, with personal access tokens and OAuth2 authorization-code flow; vendor also ships an official remote MCP server.
blocker_notes: The Greenhouse Harvest API pages refer to a different product and were ignored. The Harvest MCP help page was not among the supplied pages, so the MCP claim rests on draft evidence only.

name: Stripe
one_liner: Stripe has a broad REST API with self-serve free API keys (test mode/sandbox), OAuth via Stripe Apps/Connect, and an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: None for building and testing; sandbox keys are available with an account.

name: Plaid
one_liner: Plaid has a broad REST API with a free Sandbox for everyone; the free Production Trial is limited to US/CA signups, and full production needs approval.
blocker_notes: Sandbox is free and unlimited, so a toolkit can be built and tested without approval. The Trial plan adds free real-data access for US/CA developers. Full Production approval takes a few business days but does not block building.

name: Binance
one_liner: Binance offers a broad, free REST/WebSocket API for spot, futures, wallet and more using self-generated HMAC-signed API keys, plus an official vendor-hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Per-user API keys with HMAC signing mean there is no self-serve OAuth for multi-user access. This is a design consideration, not a blocker.

name: Paygent Connect
one_liner: Paygent Connect (gopaygent.com) is a payments platform with a REST API, bearer API keys (pgt_live_...), webhooks and a sandbox, plus a free plan. Other unrelated "Paygent" products appear in the evidence, so identity is a risk.
blocker_notes: The MCP servers in the pages belong to different products. These are api.paygent.tech (virtual cards), withpaygent.com (@paygent-ai/mcp-server, usage billing) and the paygentic-sdk GitHub repo. None of them is gopaygent.com. The gopaygent.com developer docs (https://gopaygent.com/developers/docs) were not fetched, so "none" for MCP is unverified and kept only as the draft value, with low confidence. Whether the free plan includes API keys is also unverified.

name: iPayX
one_liner: iPayX offers a Bearer-key REST FX audit API with OpenAPI 3.1, webhooks and an official MCP server; a free tier exists (documented as 10 audits/day per key on MCP; limits vary by page), narrow scope.
blocker_notes: API keys start on the $99/month Developer plan; the free tier is 5 lifetime audits in the web app.

name: QuickBooks
one_liner: QuickBooks Online has a broad REST accounting API with self-serve OAuth 2.0, a free developer account, sandbox and a free Builder tier. A production app assessment may apply, and the pages don't confirm it.
blocker_notes: Builder tier CorePlus calls are capped at 500k a month and blocked above that. Premium APIs need a paid tier. Dev and sandbox work is immediate.

name: Xero
one_liner: Xero has a broad REST accounting API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 app registration and a free Starter tier (5 connections); official hosted Remote MCP exists (Starter limited to demo org).
blocker_notes: Starter caps at 5 connections and 1,000 calls/day/org; journals endpoint needs Advanced tier with approval. Not blocking building and testing core toolkit.

name: Brex
one_liner: Brex has a broad REST API using admin-generated user tokens. Multi-user OAuth for the main API is partner-only. The vendor's official MCP server supports OAuth with dynamic client registration. The builder needs a Brex business account.
blocker_notes: The builder needs a Brex business account with admin rights to accept the developer agreement and create a token. Partner OAuth for the main API requires Brex approval. The pages did not confirm whether a sandbox exists.

name: Ramp
one_liner: Ramp has a broad REST API with OAuth2 (client credentials and authorization code), a sandbox, and an official hosted MCP server. Credentials need a Ramp admin account, and the API agreement says access requires Ramp review.
blocker_notes: Credentials need Ramp admin access and approval under the API agreement. Multi-user distribution requires publishing through the partner Developer Console.

name: PitchBook
one_liner: PitchBook has a REST API (PB-Token API key) but access is a separate contract-gated Direct Data offering via account manager; sandbox key only after engaging sales. The vendor also offers an MCP (Premium Connector / Data MCP) for licensed customers.
blocker_notes: Credentials only via a sales/contract conversation with PitchBook's Direct Data team or account manager, plus purchased API credits. Docs are public on Postman but keys are not self-serve.

name: NotebookLM
one_liner: Google has an official Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) REST API. A free Public Preview covers notebooks and sources with OAuth 2.0 user tokens. The Enterprise API needs paid licenses. Only community MCP servers exist.
blocker_notes: The API is a Preview with no SLA. It is narrow (notebooks and sources only, no chat). Workspace accounts are reportedly unsupported, per secondary sources. The draft's official MCP claim was wrong. The cited GitHub issue is only a request for an official server.

name: Otter AI
one_liner: Otter.ai has a REST public API with self-generated bearer API keys, but it's Enterprise-only and requires account-manager enablement; an official OAuth MCP server exists (mcp.otter.ai).
blocker_notes: API access requires an Enterprise plan and enablement via an Otter account manager. The official MCP server is OAuth-based with 3 tools (get user info, search, fetch), but it is not a general developer API.

name: Fathom
one_liner: Fathom (fathom.ai AI notetaker) has a free-tier REST API with user-generated API keys, OAuth2 for multi-user apps, webhooks, and an official MCP server.
blocker_notes: The rate limit is 60 calls per minute across all of a user's keys. Keys only see meetings the holder recorded or that were shared to their Team. The support.fathomhq.com (finance product) and usefathom.com (analytics) pages are different products and were ignored.

name: Consensus
one_liner: Consensus offers a self-serve REST API for scholarly paper search with a free tier (30 calls/month), API keys, OAuth 2.0 PKCE, and an official hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Free tier is limited (30 calls/month, 1 req/s) but sufficient to build and test.

name: Reducto
one_liner: Reducto offers a REST document parsing/extraction API with free self-serve signup (free credits), bearer API keys, and an official MCP server.
blocker_notes: None; free credits allow building and testing.

name: Devin
one_liner: Devin has a documented v3 REST API (sessions, playbooks, knowledge, enterprise) using cog_ bearer tokens and an official vendor-hosted MCP server at mcp.devin.ai. Whether the Free plan includes API access is unconfirmed, so a paid plan is still assumed.
blocker_notes: The builder may need a paid plan to get API credentials. This is unconfirmed, because the pages only say to sign up for a Devin account and generate an API key. Multi-user access relies on per-user PATs or service keys, not OAuth.

name: higgsfield
one_liner: Higgsfield has a REST API (api.higgsfield.ai) for 50+ image/video models using key ID:secret auth, pay-as-you-go from a $5 minimum prepaid balance with no free tier; an official OAuth MCP (tied to a paid Higgsfield subscription) also exists.
blocker_notes: Builder must top up at least $5 to get API credentials. This is a small prepaid cost, not a sales or partnership gate.

name: Mermaid CLI
one_liner: Mermaid CLI (mmdc) is a local open-source Node/Puppeteer renderer with no hosted API or credentials; the vendor's separate hosted Mermaid.ai API and official MCP server are a different product.
blocker_notes: Mermaid CLI is a local binary that depends on Puppeteer and Chromium, so there is no remote API to authenticate against. The hosted Mermaid.ai API (free accounts work) and its official MCP server are a separate product that could be evaluated on its own and would likely be ready.

name: YouTube Transcript
one_liner: TranscriptAPI is a hosted REST API for YouTube transcripts, search, channels and playlists, using self-serve Bearer API keys, with a free signup and a vendor-hosted MCP server.
blocker_notes: Signup is free and keys are self-serve. Credit limits on the free tier are unverified, but they are not an obvious blocker.

name: Grain
one_liner: Grain (grain.com) has a documented REST public API with free-plan Personal Access Tokens, OAuth2 auth-code+PKCE, webhooks, and an official remote MCP server.
blocker_notes: PATs are free and self-serve, so testing can start now. Minor uncertainty on whether OAuth app registration is self-serve.
